The previous lesson showed why dead reckoning from drive encoders drifts. Every source of error — slip, backlash, encoder resolution — adds up over time.

The solution: dedicated odometry hardware that measures ground truth more accurately and fuses data from multiple sensors.

This is where Pinpoint comes in.

The GoBILDA Pinpoint is a dedicated odometry computer — a small board with its own microcontroller (STM32) that connects to two odometry pods and an IMU.

Odometry pods are unpowered, spring-loaded wheels that ride along the ground. Because they're not driving the robot, they don't slip — they measure true ground distance.

Pinpoint runs at roughly 0.75 ms per pose update, about 1,333 Hz. Your main robot loop runs at maybe 50-100 Hz. Pinpoint is over 10x faster.

It fuses encoder data with the built-in IMU using sensor fusion algorithms, then reports a single clean pose over I2C.

content.question: Which of these is NOT an advantage of Pinpoint over hand-rolled odometry?
options: Higher update rate (1,333 Hz vs. ~50 Hz main loop)
Dedicated odometry pods reduce wheel slip error
Offloads localization processing from the main robot controller
It eliminates the need for drive motor encoders entirely

content.value:
Pinpoint returns a full 2D pose: (x, y, heading) in inches and radians.

It tracks two odometry pods — one forward/backward, one sideways — plus the IMU.

The forward pod measures forward travel. The strafe pod measures sideways travel. The IMU provides absolute heading.

Because Pinpoint runs on its own chip, it doesn't use CPU time on your main robot controller. Your OpMode just reads the latest pose whenever it needs it.

The pose is computed from three fused sensor inputs, making it much more accurate than encoder-only dead reckoning.

Pedro Pathing wraps Pinpoint into its localization layer. Instead of writing raw I2C reads, you configure PinpointConstants and let the Follower handle everything.

From the Pedro Pathing perspective, Pinpoint is just one localizer option among several — you can also use drive encoders, two-wheel, three-wheel, or other setups.

Pedro Pathing also provides DeadWheelLocalizer which tracks unpowered dead wheel odometry pods instead of dedicated hardware, useful when you don't have a Pinpoint chip.
